articles.title: Problematic pornography use is linked to craving, shame, depression, and loneliness, meta-analysis finds
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 121,728 participants finds that problematic pornography use is most strongly linked to craving and sexual shame, with smaller links to depression and loneliness. How strong these links appear may depend on the measure used.

articles.title: Women and underrepresented minorities have higher tenure-track placement rates in the political science job market
articles.summary: What actually lands a PhD student a tenure-track professorship? A new study suggests a candidate's publication record, research field, and demographic identity are much stronger predictors of hiring success than the prestige of their university.

articles.title: New study links sexual objectification at home to young women’s difficulty saying no to unwanted sex
articles.summary: New research suggests that young women who received objectifying messages from their families growing up are more likely to view themselves as objects, a mindset linked to difficulties communicating sexual desires and experiencing orgasm.

articles.title: Virtual reality can induce mystical experiences, new study suggests
articles.summary: Virtual reality headsets might offer a reliable way to induce profound feelings of unity and awe typically associated with deep spiritual practices or psychedelics, providing researchers with a new tool to study human consciousness.

articles.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how fast your brain is aging
articles.summary: A UCLA study links faster brain aging to specific gut bacteria and chemical byproducts, with older-looking brains also associated with poorer memory, focus, and mood. The findings suggest that biological signs of brain aging may appear decades before obvious symptoms and could eventually make the gut a target for prevention.

articles.title: This common vitamin could help fight one of the deadliest brain cancers
articles.summary: High-dose vitamin B3 is showing intriguing early promise as an addition to standard glioblastoma treatment, with 82% of patients in a small trial remaining progression-free after six months. Researchers believe niacin may help revive immune cells suppressed by the cancer, but larger studies are still needed to confirm the benefit and safety.

articles.title: Study of 2.5 million children finds no link between MMR vaccine and autism
articles.summary: Evaluating the health records of over 2.5 million children, researchers found no evidence that receiving the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine before age two increases the risk of a childhood autism diagnosis.

articles.title: Psychologists identify “collective anti-mattering” as a key driver of modern political grievances
articles.summary: New research shows that feeling your social group is ignored by society triggers deep anger and anxiety. These emotions can lead to political mobilization, a desire for strong leaders, and support for punitive policies.

articles.title: Americans often fail to notice when Democrats and Republicans are moving in the same direction
articles.summary: We often overestimate how divided our political opponents are from us. New research shows that highlighting shared trajectories of opinion change can soften partisan animosity, provided we don't dwell on today’s existing political gaps.

articles.title: Conscientiousness outshines cognitive ability in predicting leadership among West Point cadets
articles.summary: While test scores predict classroom success for West Point cadets, a new meta-analysis reveals that the personality trait of conscientiousness is the best indicator of future military leadership performance.

articles.title: Hormone therapy before frozen embryo transfer is tied to larger babies but not to differences in early childhood IQ
articles.summary: Children conceived through frozen embryo transfers using hormone therapy show similar early childhood intelligence scores to those conceived via natural cycles, according to a new study, despite a higher rate of unusually large babies.

articles.title: Brain scans reveal hyper-connected reward networks in autistic individuals
articles.summary: A recent brain imaging study reveals that the reward system is hyper-connected to other social networks in autistic individuals. This heightened integration correlates with social communication differences and overlaps with specific genetic and chemical markers.

articles.title: Teen cannabis use linked to flattened cognitive development in large U.S. study
articles.summary: New research indicates that adolescents who begin using cannabis may experience slower cognitive development than their non-using peers. While future users often start with slightly higher cognitive scores in late childhood, their rate of mental improvement falls behind.

articles.title: What It’s Like to Be…a Hotshot
articles.summary: Digging line to redirect the country's fiercest wildland fires, sleeping in the dirt after a 16-hour day, and turning physical endurance into a public service with Ben Strahan, a hotshot crew superintendent in California. articles.title: Psilocybin shows early promise for lingering Lyme disease symptoms

articles.title: Left-wing justifications partly shield antisemitism from liberal disapproval, study suggests
articles.summary: Political liberals strongly condemn prejudice, but new research shows this changes when antisemitism is justified by criticism of Israel. These left-leaning rationalizations act as a social shield, making the speaker appear as a political ally rather than a bigot.

articles.title: Your gut may be making a molecule that raises Alzheimer’s risk
articles.summary: Scientists have linked a gut bacterial compound called ImP to greater Alzheimer’s risk, harmful brain protein buildup, and faster cognitive decline. The finding raises the possibility that reducing ImP in the blood could one day help slow or prevent dementia.

articles.title: Could quitting ultra-processed food boost your mental health?
articles.summary: People with depression who dramatically cut ultra-processed foods experienced notable improvements in their symptoms in a small preliminary study. Researchers suspect healthier eating may benefit the brain partly by reducing gut damage and chronic inflammation.
